questions.q: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.why: Present simple is used for general facts and scientific truths.

questions.q: Quiet, please! The baby ___ right now.
questions.why: Present continuous describes an action happening at this moment.

questions.q: She usually ___ to work, but today she is taking the bus.
questions.why: Present simple describes habits and routines, signalled by 'usually'.

questions.q: Look! It ___ outside, so take an umbrella.
questions.why: Present continuous is used for actions happening now, often after 'Look!'.

questions.q: I ___ this book; it belongs to the library.
questions.why: State verbs like 'own' are not normally used in continuous tenses.

questions.q: While I ___ dinner, the phone rang.
questions.why: Past continuous sets a longer background action interrupted by a short past simple event.

questions.q: When the alarm went off, everyone ___ the building immediately.
questions.why: Past simple describes a completed action that happened at a specific past moment.

questions.q: By the time we arrived, the film ___ already ___.
questions.why: Past perfect shows an action completed before another past action.

questions.q: I couldn't get in because I ___ my keys at home.
questions.why: Past perfect describes the earlier of two past events.

questions.q: This time tomorrow I ___ on a beach in Spain.
questions.why: Future continuous describes an action in progress at a specific future time.

questions.q: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
questions.why: 'Going to' expresses a prediction based on present evidence.

questions.q: I've decided: I ___ a doctor when I grow up.
questions.why: 'Will' can express an instant decision or future intention.

questions.q: We ___ Anna tonight; we arranged it last week.
questions.why: Present continuous is used for fixed future arrangements with other people.

questions.q: The train ___ at 9:45, according to the timetable.
questions.why: Present simple is used for scheduled events and timetables.

questions.q: I ___ you a hand with those bags.
questions.why: 'Will' expresses a spontaneous offer made at the moment of speaking.

questions.q: He ___ the news because the look on his face was strange.
questions.why: 'Believe' is a state verb, so it takes past simple, not continuous.

questions.q: They ___ tennis every Sunday morning.
questions.why: Present simple is used for regular, repeated activities.

questions.q: I ___ to her for an hour when she finally apologised.
questions.why: Past perfect continuous shows the duration of an action up to a past point.

questions.q: What ___ you ___ at eight o'clock last night?
questions.why: Past continuous asks about an action in progress at a specific past time.

questions.q: I ___ that perfume; it smells wonderful.
questions.why: 'Love' is a state verb and is normally used in the simple form.

questions.q: Don't call at 7; we ___ dinner then.
questions.why: Future continuous describes being in the middle of an activity at a future time.

questions.q: She was tired because she ___ all day.
questions.why: Past perfect continuous explains a past state with a preceding ongoing action.

questions.q: As soon as the sun ___, we will set off.
questions.why: After time words like 'as soon as', use present simple for future meaning.

questions.q: I ___ about buying a new car; what do you think?
questions.why: 'Think' meaning 'consider' is an action verb and can be continuous.

questions.q: When I was a child, we ___ in a small village.
questions.why: Past simple describes a permanent past situation that is now finished.

questions.q: Be careful! You ___ that vase.
questions.why: Present continuous can describe something developing right now.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I can't talk now; I ___ (drive).'
questions.why: Present continuous describes an action happening at the moment of speaking.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'The sun ___ (rise) in the east.'
questions.why: Present simple expresses a general truth that is always the case.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'They ___ (already / finish) the project before the deadline.' (past perfect)
questions.why: Past perfect with 'already' shows completion before another past moment.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Tomorrow at noon we ___ (fly) over the Atlantic.' (future continuous)
questions.why: Future continuous describes an action in progress at a precise future time.

questions.q: By the time we arrived, the film ___.
questions.why: Past perfect for the earlier of two past events.

questions.q: This time next week I ___ on a beach.
questions.why: Future continuous for an action in progress at a future time.

questions.q: She ___ TV when the phone rang.
questions.why: Past continuous for the background action interrupted by a past simple event.

questions.q: Look at those clouds — it ___ rain.
questions.why: 'Going to' for predictions based on present evidence.

questions.q: Type the verb: 'Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.' (boil)
questions.why: Present simple for scientific facts; third person singular adds -s.
